name: Battle of Agincourt
note: The precise location of the battle is not known, and the directions are not given. The woods stand either side of the narrow open land; the accounts do not say exactly where they lay. The English stood across about 750 yards of the defile, so the plan is not to scale. The English account places the baggage attack at the start of the battle and some accounts place it near the end; it is left off the plan. The plan shows the English archers 'left' and 'right' as drawn here: the accounts do not say which of the two wings each stood on.

terrain.name: Woods of Tramecourt
terrain.quote: between the woods of Tramecourt and Azincourt

terrain.name: Woodland
terrain.quote: The recently ploughed land hemmed in by dense woodland favoured the English

units.name: English archers, left
units.quote: The archers were commanded by Sir Thomas Erpingham, another elderly veteran.

units.name: English archers, right
units.quote: the English adopted their usual battle line of longbowmen on either flank, with men-at-arms and knights in the centre

units.name: English men-at-arms
units.quote: the centre led by the king himself

units.name: French vanguard
units.quote: a vanguard up front and a main battle behind, both composed principally of men-at-arms fighting on foot

units.name: French main battle
units.quote: The dukes of Alençon and Bar led the main battle.

units.name: French dismounted left wing
units.quote: A further 600 dismounted men-at-arms stood in each wing, the left under the Count of Vendôme

units.name: French dismounted right wing
units.quote: the right under the Count of Richemont

units.name: French cavalry, left horn
units.quote: a cavalry force of 800–1,200 picked men-at-arms

units.name: French cavalry, right horn
units.quote: distributed evenly between both flanks of the vanguard (standing slightly forward, like horns)

units.name: French mounted rearguard
units.quote: the French drew up a third battle, the rearguard, which was on horseback

phases.title: The two armies are drawn up
phases.text: The English stood in three groups across the defile, with archers on the flanks and men-at-arms in the centre. The French stood in a vanguard and a main battle behind it, with dismounted men-at-arms in the wings, cavalry on the flanks of the vanguard and a mounted rearguard.
phases.quote: Early on 25 October, Henry deployed his army (approximately 1,500 men-at-arms and 7,000 longbowmen) across a 750-yard (690 m) part of the defile.

phases.title: The English move up and reset their stakes
phases.text: Henry ordered his army forward and the stakes were pulled out of the ground, carried to the new position and set again to protect the archers.
phases.quote: Henry ordered his army to advance and to start a battle that, given the state of his army, he would have preferred to avoid

phases.title: The longbowmen shoot from extreme range
phases.text: The English longbowmen began to shoot at the French from extreme range, about 300 yards. The French cavalry did not charge until after this first volley.
phases.quote: charged only after the initial volley of arrows from the English

phases.title: The French cavalry charge the archers
phases.text: The French cavalry, disorganised and not at full numbers, charged towards the longbowmen. They could not outflank the archers because of the woodland, and could not charge through the stakes.
phases.quote: The French cavalry, despite being disorganised and not at full numbers, charged towards the longbowmen.

phases.title: The wounded horses break back through the French
phases.text: The charge failed and the cavalry fell back. Wounded and panicking horses galloped through the advancing infantry, scattering and trampling it, while the vanguard walked on through the mud.
phases.quote: the wounded and panicking horses galloped through the advancing infantry, scattering them and trampling them down in their headlong flight from the battlefield.

phases.title: The French men-at-arms reach the English line
phases.text: The surviving French men-at-arms reached the front of the English line and pushed it back, while the longbowmen on the flanks went on shooting, now at close range.
phases.quote: The surviving French men-at-arms reached the front of the English line and pushed it back, while the longbowmen on the flanks continued to shoot, now at close range.

phases.title: The archers drop their bows and attack
phases.text: When their arrows ran out the archers dropped their bows and attacked the disordered, tired and wounded French men-at-arms with hatchets, swords, spears and the mallets they had used to drive in their stakes.
phases.quote: When the archers ran out of arrows, they dropped their bows and, using hatchets, swords, spears and the mallets they had used to drive their stakes in

phases.title: The second line joins and the fight is lost in the press
phases.text: The French second line joined the attack but was swallowed up, the narrow ground hampering it. The fighting lasted about three hours, until the leaders of the second line were killed or captured, as those of the first line had been.
phases.quote: As the melee developed, the French second line also joined the attack, but they too were swallowed up, the narrow terrain hampering their effectiveness.
